tips.title: Include All 10 Required Elements in a Public Notice
tips.summary: Ensure every public notice contains the EPA Public Notification Rule’s 10 mandatory elements to meet regulatory requirements and provide clear information to the public.
steps: Identify the 10 required elements: violation description, contaminant(s), timing, health effects, vulnerable populations, alternate water use, consumer actions, system response, compliance timeline, contact info.
Draft the notice incorporating each element.
Review for completeness before distribution.
warnings: Incomplete notices may violate EPA regulations and reduce public trust.
tips.evidence_excerpt: All public notices must include a clear and readily understandable explanation of each violation containing the following 10 elements from EPA’s Public Notification Rule (PNR) Quick Reference Guide.

sources.title: Preparing an Advisory Drinking Water Advisory Communications Toolbox | Water, Sanitation, & Hygiene-related Emergencies & and Outbreaks | Healthy Water | CDC

tips.title: Translate Messages Through Community Partners
tips.summary: Use trusted community partners or professional translators to produce accessible versions of advisories, avoiding automated translation tools.
steps: Identify local community organizations with language expertise.
Provide source material and context to translators.
Review translated drafts for accuracy and cultural relevance.
Distribute translated advisories via appropriate channels.
warnings: Online dictionaries or generic software can produce mistranslations that misinform the public.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Use community partners or professional translation services to translate the message. Avoid using online dictionaries or other computer software.

sources.title: Preparing an Advisory Drinking Water Advisory Communications Toolbox | Water, Sanitation, & Hygiene-related Emergencies & and Outbreaks | Healthy Water | CDC

tips.title: Employ Multiple Communication Channels
tips.summary: Disseminate advisories through a mix of traditional media, SMS, social media, and variable message signs to reach diverse audiences.
steps: Select channels based on audience demographics and message length constraints.
Prepare abbreviated messages for channels with limited space.
Schedule simultaneous releases across chosen platforms.
warnings: Relying on a single channel may leave segments of the population uninformed.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Today’s communication channels are diverse. You will likely need to consider multiple channels in addition to traditional media.

sources.title: Preparing an Advisory Drinking Water Advisory Communications Toolbox | Water, Sanitation, & Hygiene-related Emergencies & and Outbreaks | Healthy Water | CDC

tips.title: Designate and Rehearse a Credible Spokesperson
tips.summary: Choose an authoritative spokesperson and rehearse key messages to ensure consistent, trustworthy communication during an advisory.
steps: Select a spokesperson with authority, credibility, and accessibility.
Use the SOCO Worksheet and Message Mapping Template to prepare key points.
Conduct mock press briefings to rehearse responses to anticipated questions.
warnings: An unprepared spokesperson can spread misinformation and erode public confidence.
tips.evidence_excerpt: The spokesperson should be someone in authority who is honest, credible, competent, accessible, and sensitive to public concerns.

sources.title: Preparing an Advisory Drinking Water Advisory Communications Toolbox | Water, Sanitation, & Hygiene-related Emergencies & and Outbreaks | Healthy Water | CDC

tips.title: Encourage Notice Sharing
tips.summary: Include a statement urging recipients to forward the advisory to others, amplifying reach and community awareness.
steps: Add a brief encouragement line to the notice, e.g., "Please share this notice with neighbors and friends."
Place the statement prominently in the notice and digital posts.
warnings: Omitting this step may limit the advisory’s dissemination beyond initial recipients.
tips.evidence_excerpt: A statement encouraging the notice recipients to share the notice with other persons, where applicable.

sources.title: Preparing an Advisory Drinking Water Advisory Communications Toolbox | Water, Sanitation, & Hygiene-related Emergencies & and Outbreaks | Healthy Water | CDC

tips.title: Use Abbreviated Messages for Space‑Limited Channels
tips.summary: Craft concise messages that convey essential actions for channels like SMS, social media, and broadcast alerts.
steps: Identify the core action (e.g., boil water), location, contact info, and where to get more info.
Format the message to fit character limits of each channel.
Test readability before sending.
warnings: Too brief messages may omit critical safety information.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Brief messages are appropriate for: On-screen scroll, Text message systems, Social media, etc.

sources.title: Preparing an Advisory Drinking Water Advisory Communications Toolbox | Water, Sanitation, & Hygiene-related Emergencies & and Outbreaks | Healthy Water | CDC

tips.title: Customize Chemical Contaminant Advisories with Expert Input
tips.summary: When chemical contaminants are involved, consult experts and tailor messages to specific health impacts and exposure routes.
steps: Engage chemical safety experts to assess health risks and exposure pathways.
Use the Message Mapping Template and Sample Message Map to adapt the advisory language.
Include specific guidance relevant to the contaminant type.
warnings: Generic microbial advisories may not address chemical‑specific risks.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Particularly when dealing with chemical contaminants, consult with experts to understand the potential health impact and impact routes... so messages are customized to the contaminant.

tips.title: Use Local, Sustainable Materials
tips.summary: Prioritize locally sourced, sustainably harvested materials for shelter construction to reduce transport costs, environmental impact, and support local economies.
steps: Identify available local materials (wood, sand, etc.).
Assess sustainability and environmental impact.
Source materials responsibly.
Incorporate into shelter design.
warnings: Overharvesting can damage local ecosystems.
Unsustainable sourcing may increase costs.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Emergency shelter needs are best met by using locally available, sustainably sourced materials and construction methods.

sources.title: Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards | UNHCR

tips.title: Employ Plastic Sheeting as Primary Shelter Component
tips.summary: Use lightweight, UV-resistant plastic sheeting as the main covering for shelters, combined with rigid framing for flexibility and cost-effectiveness.
steps: Acquire sufficient plastic sheeting.
Attach to framing or skeleton.
Seal edges with tape or staples.
warnings: Not wind-resistant; may fail in heavy rain or high winds.
Improper disposal can harm the environment.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Plastic sheeting has become the most important shelter component in many humanitarian response operations, often in combination with rigid materials.

sources.title: Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards | UNHCR

tips.title: Adhere to Minimum Covered Living Space Standards
tips.summary: Ensure shelters provide at least 3.5 m² per person in warm climates and 4.5–5.5 m² per person in cold climates to prevent overcrowding and maintain comfort.
steps: Calculate required area per person.
Design shelter layout accordingly.
Verify compliance before occupancy.
warnings: Insufficient space leads to overcrowding and health risks.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Minimum 3.5m2 of covered living space per person in tropical or warm climates... Minimum 4.5m2 to 5.5m2 indoor living space per person in cold climates.

sources.title: Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards | UNHCR

tips.title: Maintain Minimum Shelter Height for Ventilation
tips.summary: Design shelters with a minimum of 2 m height at the lowest point to promote air circulation and reduce heat loss.
steps: Set roof height to at least 2 m.
Ensure clearance for occupants and ventilation.
Adjust design for local climate if needed.
warnings: Low height reduces airflow and can cause condensation.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Minimum height of 2m at the lowest point, with greater height being preferable to aid air circulation and ventilation.

sources.title: Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards | UNHCR

tips.title: Insulate and Seal Shelters in Cold Climates
tips.summary: Use plastic sheeting, tapes, and insulation on walls, roofs, and doors to retain heat and reduce wind and snow penetration.
steps: Seal windows and doors with plastic sheeting and tape.
Insulate walls, ceilings, and floors.
Check for gaps and seal them.
warnings: Improper sealing can lead to fire hazards if heating sources are used.
Insulation must be fire‑rated.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Windows and doors should be covered with translucent plastic sheeting and stapled on window and door frames. Walls, ceilings and floors of the living space should be designed to insulate from cold air.

sources.title: Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards | UNHCR

tips.title: Use Adequate Heating Stoves in Cold Environments
tips.summary: Deploy 5–7 kW stoves capable of heating 40–70 m² to maintain indoor temperatures of 15–19 °C, ensuring stability and clean energy use.
steps: Select a stove with 5–7 kW output.
Ensure stable installation and proper ventilation.
Use clean fuels and monitor for fire risk.
warnings: Stove instability can cause fires.
Poor ventilation can lead to carbon monoxide buildup.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Depending on conditions, a stove with 5 to 7 kW performance should have the capacity to heat a space with a floor area of 40 to 70 m2 in most cold areas.

sources.title: Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards | UNHCR

tips.summary: Quickly evaluate and repair broken water infrastructure to restore safe water supply.
steps: Conduct rapid assessment of water system damage
Identify critical repair points
Mobilize repair teams and materials
Test water quality post-repair
Communicate status to community
warnings: Requires trained personnel; risk of contamination if not properly sealed
tips.evidence_excerpt: Rapid assessment and rehabilitation of damaged water systems

Fill and test water

Procure products

tips.title: Boil Water During Advisories
tips.summary: When a boil water advisory is issued, heat water to a rolling boil for at least one minute to kill pathogens such as Cryptosporidium.
steps: Check local advisories for boil water orders.
Collect water from a safe source.
Heat water on a stove or other heat source until it reaches a rolling boil.
Maintain the boil for at least 1 minute.
Cool and store in clean containers.
Use the boiled water for drinking, cooking, and brushing teeth.
Reboil if water is stored for more than 24 hours.
warnings: Do not use water that has been stored in contaminated containers.
Avoid boiling water that may contain chemical contaminants.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Boil Water Advisories. For Cryptosporidium, but applies to other organisms as well.

tips.title: Follow Bulk Water Hauling Guidelines
tips.summary: Use the Connecticut Department of Public Health bulk water hauling guidelines to safely transport large volumes of water during emergencies.
steps: Obtain the bulk water hauling guidelines PDF.
Select appropriate containers and transport vehicles.
Ensure containers are clean and sealed.
Transport water to the destination following local regulations.
Store water in a cool, shaded area.
Label containers with contents and date.
Dispose of any contaminated water properly.
warnings: Do not transport water in containers that have previously held chemicals.
Ensure vehicles are clean to avoid contamination.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Bulk Water Hauling Guidelines. [PDF – 4 pages]

tips.title: Clean and Disinfect Water Storage Tanks
tips.summary: Use WHO guidelines to disinfect water storage tanks and tankers to prevent contamination during emergencies.
steps: Gather WHO cleaning and disinfecting guidelines PDF.
Inspect tanks for cracks or leaks.
Clean interior surfaces with soap and water.
Apply disinfectant according to WHO instructions.
Rinse thoroughly to remove residues.
Refill with clean water.
Check for any remaining contamination before use.
warnings: Do not use disinfectants that are not approved for potable water.
Avoid over‑dilution of disinfectant which reduces effectiveness.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Cleaning and Disinfecting Water Storage Tanks and Tankers. [PDF – 4 pages]

tips.title: Practice Handwashing and Diapering After Emergencies
tips.summary: Follow CDC handwashing and diapering practices to reduce disease spread in emergency settings.
steps: Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds.
Use hand sanitizer if soap is unavailable.
Set up diapering stations with clean diapers and wipes.
Dispose of diapers in sealed bags.
Clean diapering surfaces with disinfectant.
Wash hands after diapering.
warnings: Avoid using contaminated water for handwashing.
Do not reuse diapers or wipes.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Hygiene, Handwashing, Diapering. Information on good hygiene, handwashing, and diapering practices after an emergency.

tips.title: Clean Flood Water Inside and Outside the Home
tips.summary: Follow CDC cleanup guidelines to safely remove flood water and reduce health risks.
steps: Wear protective gear (gloves, boots, mask).
Remove standing water using pumps or wet vacuums.
Dispose of contaminated water in accordance with local regulations.
Clean and disinfect surfaces with EPA‑approved disinfectants.
Dry areas thoroughly to prevent mold.
Check for structural damage before re‑occupying the space.
warnings: Avoid contact with flood water that may contain sewage or chemicals.
Do not use contaminated water for cooking or drinking.
tips.evidence_excerpt: After a Hurricane or Flood: Cleanup of Flood Water. Information on cleaning up flood water inside and outside of the home.

tips.title: Handle Community Wastewater Systems After Emergencies
tips.summary: Use CDC guidance to manage community wastewater systems and minimize disease spread.
steps: Inspect systems for damage or overflow.
Seal off damaged sections to prevent contamination.
Use temporary sanitation solutions if needed.
Monitor water quality regularly.
Report any issues to local health authorities.
warnings: Do not enter contaminated wastewater areas without proper protection.
Avoid using untreated wastewater for irrigation.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Community Wastewater Systems. Information on what to do with community wastewater systems after an emergency.

tips.title: Use the Environmental Health Shelter Assessment Tool
tips.summary: Employ CDC’s 14‑area assessment form to quickly evaluate shelter conditions during emergencies.
steps: Download the Environmental Health Shelter Assessment Tool.
Conduct a rapid assessment covering food safety, water quality, sanitation, etc.
Document findings and immediate needs.
Prioritize interventions based on assessment results.
Re‑assess after changes are made.
warnings: Ensure the tool is adapted to local context before use.
Do not rely solely on the tool; use professional judgment.
tips.evidence_excerpt: CDC has developed an Environmental Health Shelter Assessment Tool to assist environmental health practitioners in conducting a rapid assessment of shelter conditions during emergencies and disasters.

tips.title: Apply Infection Control Guidance in Evacuation Centers
tips.summary: Implement CDC infection control recommendations to prevent disease spread in temporary community evacuation centers.
steps: Set up handwashing stations with soap and water.
Provide hand sanitizer where water is scarce.
Ensure proper waste disposal and sanitation facilities.
Educate residents on hygiene practices.
Monitor for signs of illness and isolate if necessary.
warnings: Do not neglect ventilation, which can spread airborne pathogens.
Avoid overcrowding of sanitation facilities.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Infection Control Guidance for Community Evacuation Centers Following Disasters. Recommendations for basic infection control guidance to prevent exposure to or transmission of infectious diseases in temporary community evacuation centers.

tips.title: Integrate Small Livestock and Aquaculture into Home Gardens
tips.summary: Adding poultry and fish to home gardens boosts protein and micronutrient intake, especially for children.
steps: Select suitable species (e.g., chickens, tilapia) that fit the local climate.
Provide clean water and proper housing to prevent disease.
Use organic waste from garden crops as feed.
Harvest eggs, meat, and fish for household consumption or sale.
Monitor animal health and adjust feeding as needed.
warnings: Ensure biosecurity to avoid disease spread.
Avoid overstocking to prevent waste and pollution.
Use safe, non-toxic feed ingredients.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Post-project evaluations found increased production of vegetables, fruits, poultry and fish among the targeted households and a decline in the rates of undernutrition in children under five years of age.

sources.title: Improving  nutrition through home gardening

tips.title: Plant Underutilized, Climate‑Resistant Crops for Micronutrients
tips.summary: Growing low‑maintenance, nutrient‑rich local species can reduce micronutrient deficiencies.
steps: Identify underutilized crops native to the region (e.g., certain leafy greens, legumes).
Prepare soil with compost or organic matter.
Plant during appropriate seasons and space for optimal growth.
Harvest when mature and incorporate into daily meals.
Share surplus with neighbors to build community resilience.
warnings: Check for local pests or diseases that may affect these crops.
Avoid planting in contaminated soils.
Ensure proper storage to prevent spoilage.
tips.evidence_excerpt: In Sri Lanka, many crops in existing home gardens are under‑utilized, meaning that these species are not widely grown, rarely found in the market and not cultivated commercially, yet are low maintenance, climate resistant and contain high amounts of micronutrients.

sources.title: Improving  nutrition through home gardening

tips.title: Maximize Food Production on Small Plots
tips.summary: Even a modest garden can significantly improve household nutrition if managed well.
steps: Design a layout that maximizes sun exposure and water use.
Use crop rotation and intercropping to maintain soil fertility.
Apply compost or organic fertilizers to enrich soil.
Implement drip or mulch irrigation to conserve water.
Harvest regularly to encourage continuous production.
warnings: Avoid overuse of chemical fertilizers that can contaminate water.
Monitor soil pH and adjust as needed.
Prevent erosion on sloped plots.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Even a small plot of land, if well managed, can make a substantial contribution towards meeting household food needs and improving nutrition.

sources.title: Improving  nutrition through home gardening

tips.title: Leverage Home Gardens for Income Generation
tips.summary: Surplus produce from home gardens can create local income streams and support food security.
steps: Grow a mix of high‑value crops (e.g., herbs, tomatoes).
Establish a small market stall or community sales group.
Use fair pricing and promote fresh, local produce.
Reinvest profits into garden improvements or livestock.
Track sales to identify best‑selling items.
warnings: Ensure compliance with local market regulations.
Avoid over‑harvesting that depletes the garden.
Protect produce from pests during transport.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Home gardens in enhancing food security by providing direct access to a variety of nutritionally rich foods, as well as employment and income generation opportunities to households.

tips.title: Promote Year‑Round Nutritional Diets through Community Gardening
tips.summary: Community‑based home gardening programs support continuous access to diverse, nutritious foods.
steps: Organize training workshops for local households.
Create shared garden plots or cooperative plots.
Develop a schedule for planting, harvesting, and storage.
Encourage participation of all age groups, especially children.
Monitor nutritional outcomes and adjust practices.
warnings: Ensure equitable access to garden space.
Prevent conflicts over resource allocation.
Maintain hygiene to avoid foodborne illnesses.
tips.evidence_excerpt: Effective community‑based action aimed at improving household food security and promoting the year‑round consumption of nutritionally adequate diets.

tips.title: Use Home Gardens to Combat Micronutrient Deficiencies
tips.summary: Diversifying fruit and vegetable production in home gardens can sustainably reduce micronutrient gaps.
steps: Select a variety of colorful fruits and vegetables rich in vitamins and minerals.
Plant in succession to provide continuous harvests.
Educate families on the nutritional benefits of each crop.
Incorporate home‑grown produce into daily meals.
Track changes in dietary diversity and health indicators.
warnings: Avoid over‑use of pesticides that may reduce nutrient quality.
Ensure safe irrigation water to prevent contamination.
Be mindful of seasonal availability of certain crops.
tips.evidence_excerpt: The policy brief suggests that promoting cultivation, harvesting and consumption of these under‑utilized food crops in home gardens is a feasible strategy to sustainably reduce micronutrient deficiencies.

tips.title: Define Clear Objectives for Your Home Garden
tips.summary: List the main outputs you want and the constraints you face to guide improvement decisions.
steps: Write a list of the main things you want your home garden to produce.
Identify major constraints such as wild pigs, poor soil or sloping land.
tips.evidence_excerpt: STEP 2: SET OBJECTIVES Make a list of the main things you want your home garden to produce. You should also identify the major constraints you need to overcome, such as wild pigs, poor soil or sloping land.

tips.title: Avoid Crossing Flooded Roads or Walkways
tips.summary: If you encounter a flooded road or walkway, do not cross; instead turn around to avoid drowning.
steps: If you approach a flooded road or walkway, turn around and do not cross.
prerequisites: Presence of a flooded road or walkway
failure_modes: Ignoring the rule and crossing the flooded area.
tips.evidence_excerpt: If you approach a flooded road or walkway, follow this rule: turn around, don't drown!
